Where \left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x .$ If $f$ is continuous on $R$, then \left(a + b\right) is equal to:

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}\sin x - e^{x} & ifx \le 0 \\ a + \left[-x\right] & if0 < x < 1 \\ 2x - b & ifx \ge 1\end{cases}$\right$

If~$f \left(x\right)$~is continuous at~$x = a$~then~$\lim_{x \to a^{-}}f \left(x\right) = f \left(a\right) = \lim_{x \to a^{+}}f\left(x\right)$.

Continuous at $x = 0$

$f \left({0}^{+}\right) =$f \left({0}^{-}\right)$

$⇒ a - 1 = 0 - e^{0}$

$⇒ a = 0$

Continuous at $x = 1$

$f \left({1}^{+}\right) =$f \left({1}^{-}\right)

$⇒ 2 \left($1\right) - b = a + \left(-1\right)$

$⇒ b = 2 - a + 1$

$⇒ b = 3$

$∴ a + b = 3

$

questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = max\left\{1 + x + \left[x\right], 2 + x, x + 2\left[x\right]\right\}, 0 \le x \le 2$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}max\left\{x + 1, x + 2, x\right\} & 0 \le x < 1 \\ max \left\{x + 2, x + 2, x + 2\right\} & 1 ≤ x < 2 \\ max\left\{5, 4, 6\right\} & x = 2\end{cases}$\right$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x + 2, & 0 \le x < 1 \\ x + 2, & 1 \le x < 2 \\ 6, & x = 2\end{cases}$\right$

$⇒ f ( x ) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x + 2 & 0 \le x < 2 \\ 6 & x = 2\end{cases}$\right$

So,~$f$~is not continuous at $x = 2$~as~$f \left({2}^{-}\right) =4 \text{ and } f \left($2\right) = 6$

And~$f$~is differentiable in \left($0, 2\right)$~as~$x + 2$~is a linear function,

$∴ m = 1, n = 0$

$⇒ \left($m + n\right)2 + 2 = 1 + 2 = 3$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.solution:
$\because f(x+y)=f(x) \cdot f(y)+f(x) \cdot f(y), \forall x, y \in R$ ....(i)$
And f(0)=1$ ....(ii)
Now replace $x$ by zero and $y$ by zero we get
$\begin{aligned}
& f(0)=f(0) f(0)+f(0) f(0) \\
& 1=f(0)+f(0) \\
& \therefore \quad f^{\prime}(0)=\frac{1}{2} ...(iii)
\end{aligned}$
Now replace $y$ by zero in equation (i), we get
$f(x)=\frac{1}{2} f(x)+f^{\prime}(x)$
or, $\frac{1}{2} f(x)=f^{\prime}(x)$
then $\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=\frac{1}{2}$
hence $\ln |f(x)|=\frac{x}{2}+c$
Put $x=0$, we get $c=0\therefore \quad \ln |f(x)|=\frac{x}{2}$
Then $\sum_{n=1}^{100} \ln (f(\eta))=\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{2}+\frac{3}{2}+\ldots+\frac{100}{2}\right)=\frac{5050}{2}=2525$

questions.solution:
Given functional equality is

Put $x = y + h,$ we get

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{f\left(y + h\right) - f ( y )}{h}\right| \le 2{\left|h\right|}^{1 / 2}$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0} \left|\dfrac{f\left(y + h\right) - f\left(y\right)}{h}\right| \le \lim_{h \to 0} 2{\left|h\right|}^{1 / 2}$

$⇒ \left|f^{′}\left(y\right)\right| \le 0$

$⇒ \left|f^{′}\left(y\right)\right| = 0$

$⇒ f′\left(y\right) = 0$

$⇒ f\left(y\right) = c$

$⇒ f\left(y\right) = 1$ (since $f\left(0\right) = 1$ )

Now ${∫}_{0}^{1}f^{2}\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{1}1dx = 1$.

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) =  \left[x^{2} - x\right] + \left|-$x + \left[x\right]\right|$, where $x \in \mathbb{R}$and \left[t\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then, $f is$
options: continuous at $x = 0$, but not continuous at $x = 1$
continuous at $x = 1$, but not continuous at $x = 0$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left[x^{2} - x\right] + \left|- x + \left[x\right]\right|$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left[x^{2} - x\right] + \left|x - \left[x\right]\right|, \left\{\text{as}\left|- A\right| = \left|A\right|\right\}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left[x^{2} - x\right] + \left|\left\{x\right\}\right|, \left\{\text{as}\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\} = x\right\}$~

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left[x^{2} - x\right] + \left\{x\right\} ( ∵ \left\{x\right\} \ge 0 )$

Now at~$x = 0$,~$f\left(0\right) = 0$

And $f\left({0}^{+}\right) = - 1, \left\{\text{as}x^{2} - x < 0\text{for}x \to {0}^{+}\right\}$

So, function is~discontinuous at~$x = 0$

Now at $x = 1$,~$f\left(1\right) = 0$,~

$f\left({1}^{+}\right) = 0 + 0 = 0$~and $f\left({1}^{-}\right) = - 1 + 1 = 0$

Hence, the function is continuous at~$x = 1$.
